emergent_bug.violated_requirement: rho = atomic([READ sk_backlog.len @tcp_space:1383]) from thread_b (single-access read that assumes no concurrent conflicting write)
emergent_bug.violating_event: e@tcp_add_backlog:1741 = sk->sk_backlog.len += delta executed in BH/softirq context, concurrent with the process-context read
emergent_bug.missing_guarantee: the BH writer updates backlog.len under bh_lock_sock (sk->sk_lock.slock); the process-context reader (during backlog drain via tcp_space) reads it locklessly without taking that spinlock, so no common lock serializes the read against the BH write
emergent_bug.category_rationale: rho = atomic(single access) on a scalar broken by a concurrent unsynchronized BH write -> KCSAN data race (a torn/stale backlog-length read)

fix_maps_to: patch adds READ_ONCE(sk->sk_backlog.len) at the reader sites (tcp_space and several diagnostic readers in sock.c/sctp/diag.c/tipc/socket.c); the commit explicitly only silences the read side and punts WRITE_ONCE on the writer. It adds NO serialize/order/counts guarantee -- it is a marked-access 'silence KCSAN' annotation, not real synchronization.
recall_risk_notes: Benign single-field torn-read race explicitly fixed by READ_ONCE (commit title: 'silence KCSAN warnings about sk->sk_backlog.len reads'), squarely the marked-access/weak-memory boundary case. The reader tolerates a stale value (tcp_space feeds a window-growth heuristic), so there is no SC ordering invariant -- just an unmarked-access KCSAN finding; the design's anti-pure-syntactic-race stance (4.6.3) means it likely won't raise or will treat it as benign. Additional risks: (1) thread_b's read sits behind a deep cross-file chain release_sock->__release_sock->tcp_v4_do_rcv->tcp_rcv_established->tcp_event_data_recv->tcp_grow_window->tcp_space(inline header), so the same sk must be threaded across files to a header-inline read; (2) cross-context MHP (softirq BH writer vs process-context reader) must be modeled, and the writer DOES hold bh_lock_sock, so the keep/reject must conclude the reader lacks that common spinlock.
